teaser.text: The central thing Schwab sells is a connected relationship for investing, borrowing, advice and financial administration. It lets one customer bring several money decisions into the same system, while Schwab earns from the balances and services around that relationship.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Schwab?

paragraphs.text: Persistent cash sorting during 2027–2029 would move the forecast toward bear by weakening deposits, net interest margin, earnings, and buybacks. Market weakness or slower asset gathering would pressure fee revenue and the multiple. An expense miss would undermine the 800-basis-point operating-leverage promise.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Schwab really make?

paragraphs.text: Schwab’s cash flow is substantial, but customer and regulatory movements make it unlike an industrial company’s cash flow. Operating cash less capital spending is a useful starting point, and stock compensation should also be treated as an economic cost because shareholders absorb the dilution.

The warning is clearest in 2023. Operating cash was far above net income because Schwab released US$23,759 million from investments segregated for regulatory purposes. That cash was real, but it reflected a balance-sheet movement rather than a surge in ordinary service revenue.

blocks.heading: How much does Schwab pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise gradually in the base case because earnings and funding conditions improve, but the forecast does not repeat the latest increase. The base dividend reaches $1.36 per share in 2027 and $1.52 in 2029. The bear case holds at $1.28, consistent with a pause during stress. The bull case reaches $1.80, requiring stronger earnings and adequate bank capital.

blocks.heading: Does Schwab's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow was $1,202 million in 2021 against dividends of $1,366 million. In 2022, dividends and buybacks reached $4,986 million against free cash flow of $1,086 million. But financial-institution cash flow is not a steady earnings pot: client deposits move, securities mature, and funding needs change. A large inflow may therefore be needed for withdrawals or debt repayment rather than dividends.

blocks.heading: What is Schwab's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The tables show a sharp earnings turn: revenue fell 9.3% in 2023, then grew 22.0% in 2025. Diluted EPS rose from $2.54 in 2023 to $4.65 in 2025. Trailing P/E is 16.1x; forward P/E is 11.7x. Dividend yield is 1.4%; buyback yield is 4.5%. Shareholder returns compete with investment and balance-sheet demands. The company’s own free cash flow was 3.5% of revenue in 2022 and 98.6% in 2023, when a large regulatory-investment release inflated operating cash. Buybacks were $7,346 million in 2025; average diluted shares fell 1.4%.

Charles Schwab Corporation is a financial-services company that combines brokerage, managed investing, banking, and services for independent advisers. At $94.16 a share on October 16, 2026, its stock looks inexpensive only if recent earnings and a demanding forecast can hold.

earnings.title: Schwab earnings
earnings.meta_description: Schwab's next results are expected January 20, 2027; guidance centers on revenue growth, funding costs, expenses and operating leverage.
earnings.opening: Schwab's next results are expected on January 20, 2027. Watch whether client cash funds growth without pushing up borrowing costs.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Schwab's business works, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks could change the outlook.

paragraphs.text: Schwab’s revenue-growth range remains 17.5%–18.5%, although Mike Verdeschi said growth should land toward the lower end. Adjusted expense growth should also finish near the bottom of its 9.5%–10.5% range. “Adjusted” removes specified items such as acquisition costs and acquired-intangible amortization, making recurring operations easier to compare, but Schwab still incurs those costs.

Net interest margin is the interest Schwab keeps after paying depositors and other funders. In the first half of 2026, Schwab reported a 3.54% yield on interest-earning assets. Its funding cost was 0.60%, leaving a 2.94% margin. Management expects a full-year margin of 3.0%–3.1%, with the lower end now more likely, but its fourth-quarter range is 3.2%–3.3%.

blocks.heading: Has Schwab kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management also has a record of keeping promises. It said the Ameritrade client transition would produce approximately US$500 million of additional annual savings beyond acquisition synergies. The final conversion finished in May 2024, and later reporting said those savings were realized. In 2025, core net new assets reached US$519.4 billion, showing growth after the technology migration.

blocks.heading: How have Schwab's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: September 2026 extended Schwab’s earnings recovery. Revenue rose 16.9% year over year. Pretax profit rose 25.0%, while diluted EPS also increased strongly.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Schwab's next results?

paragraphs.text: The December quarter comes first. Compare revenue growth, net interest margin and adjusted expenses with management’s ranges, then ask whether the promised operating leverage appeared. Year-end client cash inflows could help fund lending, but if loans grow faster than deposits, more expensive borrowing may absorb part of the interest benefit.
